answer.main_body: railway buffer stop beam and base
answer.evidence: The north-south buffer stop assembly shows a clear 3px tall horizontal top surface on its base (rows 22-24) above the 5px south-facing vertical face (rows 25-29), with the beam top extending northwards in proper 3/4 perspective.

The north-south running wooden beam correctly displays its foreshortened horizontal top surface extending from row 4 to row 21 (about 18 rows), ending at a vertical south-facing front face from row 24 to 29. There are no receding isometric side faces.

answer.main_body: railway buffer stop beam and support
answer.evidence: The north-south crossbeam correctly displays its top surface foreshortened along rows 4-21 (around 17 rows) and its south-facing vertical base/face on rows 24-29 (6 rows tall), matching standard top-down 3/4 RPG perspective.

The entire structure is drawn as a flat elevation without visible depth; the top edge at rows 4-6 provides only a 2px cap/rim, lacking the required foreshortened top surface for a 3/4 perspective standing object.
